findings.suggestion: Scope the relaxation: keep `is_triage_record` strict for its existing callers and apply the lenient check (or the normalize helper) only in the append path, or introduce a `strict=` flag with old behavior default.

findings.finding: default=argparse.SUPPRESS` on the subparser-level `--project-root` handles "before and after" but SUPPRESS means the attribute is absent when the flag isn't given — any existing code doing `args.project_root` unconditionally will raise AttributeError. findings.finding: New lib helper `triage_status_normalize.initial_record` is fine, but confirm it's actually shared (append path + import path or future callers) rather than a single-use wrapper around a two-line `status or 'triage'` — if single-use, inlining with a comment is simpler than a new module surface.
findings.suggestion: If only the append path uses it, inline it; keep the helper only if read_all_items and append both call it.

findings.finding: "Unknown status resolves to 'triage' with an integrity warning" — is "unknown" a closed allowlist (triage/snoozed/…)? If the status vocabulary grows, the allowlist in the helper must be defined once, not duplicated with `is_triage_record`'s set.
findings.suggestion: Define the status vocabulary as a single constant both functions reference. findings.suggestion: Explicitly preserve a non-blocking result and add an integration test showing that a known triage/snoozed match produces a MEDIUM finding without failing the gate.

findings.finding: The reported measurement uses the last 1,500 commits, which does not demonstrate the required release-tag range or 500-commit fallback. “20 tokens” also does not establish the audit’s actual finding count.
findings.suggestion: Run the implemented check against this repository before merge. Record the selected tag/range, print when the fallback is used, and report the resulting finding count.

findings.finding: Relaxing `is_triage_record` and normalizing during pass 1 can affect record classification and replay. The plan does not pin that only append records receive the fallback or that subsequent status updates still override it.
findings.suggestion: Add cases for missing/null/unknown append status followed by a valid update; verify the final status and integrity warning. Preserve existing corruption handling for malformed records and invalid non-append operations.

findings.finding: The CLI step omits the explicitly required test where `--project-root` appears in both positions. `SUPPRESS` prevents an absent subparser argument from overwriting the root value, but precedence when both are supplied still needs pinning.
findings.suggestion: Test before-only, after-only, and both with different paths; document and assert which path wins.  The approach is appropriately scoped and the helper extraction fits the stated bloat constraint. Address the report-only guarantee, required measurement, and targeted regression cases before approval.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: The test only asserts `"G" in audit_detector._GROUPS`. Group G was registered before this change too, so the test passes even if `group_g4` were never wired into `_group_g_combined` (or if the combined wrapper were deleted and the old `group_g.run` registered directly). It validates nothing about the new registration.
findings.suggestion: Assert that the registered "G" callable is the combined wrapper, or that a seeded G4 finding surfaces through `audit_detector` end-to-end (e.g., run the detector against the `_repo(..., None)` fixture and check a G4 finding appears).

findings.finding: When the append line has no `id` key, `item_id` becomes the string `"None"` and is used both in the warning and the `_WARNED` dedupe key. Two different malformed records both missing ids collapse to one warning. Minor, but the message `append 'None'` is misleading.
findings.suggestion: Guard with `isinstance(item.get("id"), str)` before warning/deduping, or surface the record's `ts`/`title` in the message instead.

findings.finding: sp.add_argument("--project-root", ...)` is added unconditionally to every subparser. If any existing subcommand (e.g., `amend`, or a future `list` variant) already defines `--project-root`, argparse raises `ArgumentError` at parser build time and the whole CLI dies. The tests only exercise `list`.
findings.suggestion: Skip subparsers that already define the option (check `sp._option_string_actions`), or at least add a smoke test that builds the parser and parses one arg per subcommand.

findings.finding: A partial close in the middle of a list silently truncates the token list: `"Closes trg-A, trg-B (first half)"` yields `[trg-A]` — trg-A is reported even though the commit author may have meant a mixed close. The spec only pins the list-starts-with-partial case, so this is a defined-but-undocumented gap; a commit like this produces a finding on A that the convention `Part of trg-X` was designed to avoid.
findings.suggestion: Either document this behavior in the grammar note in `docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md`, or, if a partial appears anywhere in a matched token group, drop the whole group (consistent with the conservative starts-with-partial rule).

findings.finding: git_log_scan._run_git(...).strip()` will raise `AttributeError` if `_run_git` returns bytes on any code path; the surrounding `except Exception: pass` swallows it silently, so the shallow-clone annotation is lost rather than the spec's "a shallow clone is named in the detail". Swallowing is safe for findings but hides the lost annotation.
findings.suggestion: Degrade explicitly (`except Exception: scope += ", shallow-clone check unavailable"` or log) so the known-limit annotation failure is visible.  Verified non-issues worth noting: the regex genuinely returns `[]` for a list starting with a partial id (the lookahead kills the first id and no restart point exists after the verb); the SUPPRESS-default subparser trick correctly preserves the pre-verb value and lets the post-verb value win (AC2 fully covered, including both-given and cwd-default); the GC resolver and reader now share `initial_record` so AC3's agreement is structural, not incidental; the changed `test_triage_expected_status.py` test would fail under the old behavior (`mark_status` previously raised `StatusPreconditionError`), so it's a real behavioral test.  Overall: the three ACs are implemented and mostly pinned by tests that fail on regressions; findings are refinements. Ship-with-fixes at most — the registry test is the one I'd insist on.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve

findings.finding: The ID pattern has no trailing boundary, so `Fixes trg-aaaaaaaa0` is parsed as closing `trg-aaaaaaaa`. If that eight-digit card exists and is open, G4 reports a false finding; otherwise it emits an incorrect unknown-ID line. This violates the grammar requiring an eight-hex-digit ID.
findings.suggestion: Add a trailing identifier boundary to `_ID` so longer identifiers cannot match a valid prefix. Add negative fixtures for nine-digit IDs and IDs followed by identifier characters, including within closing lists.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The diff appears to cover all three acceptance criteria, but the token parser needs this correction before shipping.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
